EVALUATION CRITERIA: auto-generated comments, repetitive numeric names (test0,test1,test7), EvoSuite artifacts. DECISION: Presence of imports referencing EvoSuite and a numeric test name 'test7' indicate generated-origin patterns. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD). RATIONALE: Test-first/BDD improves coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming. DECISION: The method includes a '// Given/When:' comment and class-level notes saying tests follow Given-When-Then, indicating deliberate design intent. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on public API and avoid implementation coupling. RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are maintainable. EVALUATION CRITERIA: absence of reflection or private-field inspection. DECISION: The test uses only public constructor and numVertices() API; no reflection or access to internals. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions with messages. RATIONALE: Descriptive assertions ease diagnosis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of messages and specific asserts. DECISION: assertEquals includes a descriptive failure message; specific assertion used. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain "why" and be minimal. RATIONALE: Good comments help diagnose complex logic. EVALUATION CRITERIA: absence of commented-out code and excessive comments. DECISION: Test contains brief Given/When comment and class-level Javadoc; no commented-out code or excessive inline comments. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must avoid non-determinism (random, current time). RATIONALE: Deterministic tests are reliable in CI. EVALUATION CRITERIA: absence of Random/System.currentTimeMillis/Thread.sleep. DECISION: No sources of non-determinism used in the method. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not create persistent side effects. RATIONALE: Prevent inter-test dependencies. EVALUATION CRITERIA: use of @After cleanup or only local variables. DECISION: This test uses only local variables and does not persist data or modify static state. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: presence of @Tag/@Category annotations. DECISION: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), satisfying this practice. VERDICT: compliant.

The method focuses on a single behavior: obtaining the transpose of a graph. There is one Arrange (create graph, insert edge), one Act (grafoTransposto()), and assertions that relate to the single behavior (distinct object and vertex count). No multiple unrelated Act operations are present.

The test uses only local variables and does not rely on shared static or instance state. There are no @Before/@After methods required for this single test and no evidence of inter-test dependencies in the method itself.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path scenario is covered. There is no test for exceptional flows (no assertThrows/@Test(expected=...) or other checks for invalid inputs or error handling), and the class contains only this one test method.

The test uses typical values (a large vertex count and an inserted edge) but does not explicitly exercise clear boundary values such as zero vertices, minimum/maximum indices or off-by-one cases. The presence of -1 as a weight is not sufficient to demonstrate systematic boundary testing.

The test contains multiple, relevant assertions (assertNotSame and assertEquals) that verify different aspects of the transpose behavior (object identity and vertex count), increasing fault detection beyond a single superficial assertion.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations and no commented-out test methods in the method shown. The test is active and runnable.
